label: Port
_model: Settlement kernel on the water. The appetite belongs to the harbour, which is a place people are always about to leave — so every cruelty here is a way of stopping them, and every prize is something that makes leaving possible again.

appetites.want: never to have an empty berth
appetites.purpose: there would always be something alongside

appeasement.move: land something on the quay, anything, and enter it

appetites.want: that everything which sails from it should come back to it
appetites.purpose: nothing would ever be lost to somewhere else

appeasement.move: come back to a place in this harbour you have already been

appetites.want: that nothing should ever fail to move when it says

appeasement.move: do one thing exactly when the harbour says, and not a moment after

appetites.want: that nothing should ever be lost within sight of it

appeasement.move: name one thing the sea took, out loud, and where it went down

accommodations.text: shipped {conscript} out on a bottom that was never coming back
pressed {conscript} aboard and would not sign them off again
held {conscript}'s goods in bond until there was nothing left to redeem them with
kept {conscript}'s ship in the harbour and never cleared her
showed {conscript} a light that was not where they took it to be
lodged {conscript} on the low quay, where the tide comes over

manifest.label: the manifest of the last ship to clear
manifest.function: the only complete account of what left here and with whom

light.label: the lamp out of the harbour light
light.function: the only thing that ever brought anything home

glass.label: the tide glass, still running
glass.function: the only clock here the water agreed with

bell.label: the bell off the ship that went down in the roads
bell.function: the only marker over what the harbour lost

factions.name: the Harbour Board
factions.essence: still clearing, still entering, still refusing to sign anything off

factions.name: the crews
factions.essence: came ashore for a night and the ship never sailed

factions.name: the Trinity Brethren
factions.essence: still keeping a light for ships that are not coming

factions.name: what comes in on the tide

triggerGlossary.announced: came along the quay in the open and were hailed
triggerGlossary.seenTwice: seen from the water twice, from different berths
triggerGlossary.loud: a raised voice across water, which carries further than you think
triggerGlossary.lingering: stayed alongside long enough to be entered as a vessel in port
triggerGlossary.disturbed: cast off a line, opened a hatch, or moved something off the tideline

foes.name: Bandit
foes.note: wreckers; they take from the drowned and would rather not fight the living

skirmish.avoid: give them something off the tideline and they take it and go

fight.line: 4 Bandits and a Hobgoblin Soldier as bailiff's man

foes.name: Bandit
foes.note: scatter if the bailiff's man drops

foes.name: Hobgoblin Soldier
foes.note: demands your papers before it strikes

fight.avoid: show it any paper with a seal on it and it stands down to read

battle.line: 1 Wraith of the Quay Master and 4 Skeletons of a drowned crew

foes.name: Wraith
foes.note: INCORPOREAL — chill touch ignores armour, drains 1 max Grit

foes.name: Skeleton
foes.note: fearless; still working the ship they died on

battle.harmedBy: blessed, silvered or magical weapons for the Wraith ONLY; anything for the Skeletons — say so before initiative
battle.avoid: it wants the crew accounted for; name one of the drowned and it stops to enter them

nightmare.line: 1 Wraith, 1 Ogre out of the mud berth and 5 Skeletons

foes.name: Ogre
foes.note: came in on a tide and was never entered anywhere

nightmare.harmedBy: blessed, silvered or magical weapons for the Wraith ONLY; anything for the rest
nightmare.avoid: do not run this without an appeasement route open

cargo.dangerLine: the quay is still working, and it does not care that there is nothing to work on

institution: warehouses running the length of the quay, all of them full
a bond store with the goods held and the duty unpaid
ritual: a manifest checked against the hold before anything is signed
goods weighed off at the quay edge and entered
the day's landings read back at the office each evening
demand: a sling loaded and hanging over an empty hold
a berth swept clean with the bollards polished
a manifest with a line left open at the bottom
wound: a warehouse packed with cargo nobody ever claimed
bond store doors sealed on goods that rotted
a crane left slewed over the water with the load down
anchor: the manifest of the last ship to clear
a bond book listing every hold and its duty

features: a sling hanging loaded over nothing
a berth swept with the bollards bright
a manifest open at a blank line
a bond seal broken and refixed
cargo stacked and unclaimed
a crane slewed out over the water

decisions.cue: a manifest with a line left open at the bottom
decisions.cost: entering something makes it landed here, on your account

resolve.success: you enter something plausible and the Board treats you as a shipper in good standing
resolve.failure: you enter it wrongly and the duty falls on you: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave the line open; the ship is not cleared and neither are you

decisions.cue: a sling loaded and hanging over an empty hold
decisions.cost: lowering it lands the cargo; cutting it loses it

resolve.success: you land it properly and the quay works for you — the crane and the crews are yours
resolve.failure: the sling parts and the load goes into the water: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: leave it hanging; it hangs over the berth you have to cross

decisions.cue: a bond store sealed on goods that were never redeemed
decisions.cost: the seal is the Custom House's, not the owner's

resolve.success: you find whose goods were bonded and can trade what they need for what you need
resolve.failure: you break the seal and the Custom House has you for smuggling: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it sealed; whatever is in there stays in there

decisions.cue: a warehouse packed to the roof with cargo nobody claimed
decisions.cost: the marks on the bales say who shipped it

resolve.success: you read the marks and learn where the last ships were bound and why
resolve.failure: you shift a bale and bring the stack down on the aisle behind you
resolve.orElse: leave the warehouse; the shipping marks are the only trail there is

decisions.cue: a berth swept clean with the bollards polished and nothing alongside
decisions.cost: tying up in it makes you a vessel in port

resolve.success: you make fast properly and the harbour enters you, and gives you a berth's protections
resolve.failure: you tie up and cannot be cleared to leave: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: stay off the berth; the quay will not work for you at all

decisions.cue: a crane left slewed out over the water with the load still down
decisions.cost: bringing it in recovers what is on the hook

resolve.success: you bring the load in and it is what somebody has been waiting years for
resolve.failure: the crane runs away with itself and takes the quay edge with it
resolve.orElse: leave it slewed; the thing on the hook stays under the water

situations.doing: checking a manifest against a hold with nothing in it
situations.onArrival: they run a finger down the page and look up at you
situations.because: the tally must agree and there is nothing to tally
situations.offer: give them one item for the list and they will clear you for anything

situations.doing: swinging an empty sling over a berth, over and over
situations.onArrival: it stops the sling in front of you at chest height
situations.because: the load was never landed and the shift never ended
situations.offer: put anything in the sling and it will lift you anywhere along the quay

situations.doing: counting bales in a warehouse that is already counted
situations.onArrival: they ask whether you are here for the consignment
situations.because: the goods were never claimed and they cannot leave until they are
situations.offer: claim the consignment and they will hand you the shipping marks

situations.doing: standing at an empty berth with a fender in his hands
situations.onArrival: he asks when she is expected
situations.because: nothing has come alongside since and the berth is kept ready
situations.offer: tell him she is coming and he will open the bond store

situations.doing: standing on the quay with the marks fresh and the ropes tight
situations.onArrival: the ropes creak as though something has just been added
situations.because: it was landed and never entered, so it cannot be moved
situations.offer: enter it on a manifest and the whole quay begins working again

situations.doing: standing sealed with the doors sweating
situations.onArrival: something inside shifts its weight when you stop walking
situations.because: the duty was never paid and the doors were never opened
situations.offer: pay something toward the duty and it opens, and gives up what it holds

temptations.cue: a page off the last manifest
temptations.benefit: once, prove a thing was landed here lawfully
temptations.standingDrawback: the Custom House checks the entry, eventually

temptations.benefit: open anything held in bond here
temptations.standingDrawback: the duty on it becomes yours, and it compounds

temptations.benefit: once, make a thing appear to belong to somebody powerful
temptations.standingDrawback: they find out that their mark is at large

temptations.benefit: once, lift or lower anything you can rig
temptations.standingDrawback: whatever you lift, the quay enters against you

temptations.benefit: once, have exactly the trade goods you need
temptations.standingDrawback: it was claimed, by somebody still looking

passage.dangerLine: everything here is about to leave and none of it ever does

institution: a harbour office where every clearance is signed before a ship may sail
a pilot company that takes every vessel out and brings it back
a light kept burning at the harbour mouth
ritual: a ship cleared outward and her papers stamped at the gate
the pilot taken aboard at the bar and put off outside it
a lamp lit at dusk whether or not anything is expected
demand: a clearance made out and unstamped on a desk
a pilot boat lying off with the oars shipped and nobody in her
wound: clearances refused in a single day, every one of them
a pilot stair with the bottom steps gone
the light kept burning for a ship that had already gone down
anchor: the lamp out of the harbour light
a book of clearances with every sailing entered
a chart of the bar that has never been wrong

features: a clearance made out and unstamped
a pilot boat lying off, empty
a lamp burning in daylight
a pilot stair missing its bottom steps
a chart of the bar left open
a sea chest packed and corded

decisions.cue: a clearance made out and never stamped
decisions.cost: stamping it lets something sail

resolve.success: you stamp it properly and one thing here is finally released, and it repays you
resolve.failure: you stamp it blind and have cleared something that should have stayed: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it unstamped; nothing here can leave, including you

decisions.cue: a lamp burning in the harbour light at noon
decisions.cost: putting it out ends the watch; keeping it lit continues it

resolve.success: you learn what the light is being kept for and can answer it
resolve.failure: you put it out and something loses its way in, badly: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: leave it burning; it goes on calling, and things go on coming

decisions.cue: a pilot boat lying off the stair with her oars shipped and nobody aboard
decisions.cost: taking her out means crossing the bar

resolve.success: you take her out and can move on the water, which nothing ashore can follow
resolve.failure: you take her out on the wrong tide and are set down on the bar
resolve.orElse: stay ashore; every route from here is along the quay, in the open

decisions.cue: a pilot stair with the bottom steps gone
decisions.cost: the missing steps were taken, not worn

resolve.success: you find where the steps went and what was being kept from the water
resolve.failure: you go down anyway and the stair puts you in the mud at low water
resolve.orElse: use the next stair along, costing a Turn

decisions.cue: a chart of the bar with a sounding altered in a different hand
decisions.cost: the alteration put a ship on the sand

resolve.success: you find who altered it and can prove what was done to whom
resolve.failure: you take the chart as read and trust a channel that is not there
resolve.orElse: leave the chart; you have no proof of the transgression at the ending

decisions.cue: a sea chest packed and corded at the head of the stair
decisions.cost: somebody was leaving and did not

resolve.success: you open it and learn who was going, and where, and what they were taking
resolve.failure: you shoulder it and the harbour takes you for them: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave the chest; whoever it belonged to is not identified

situations.doing: standing at the head of the stair with a bag over his shoulder
situations.onArrival: he asks whether you are the ship he is taking out
situations.because: he was called for a vessel that never came to the bar
situations.offer: tell him you are and he will take you over the bar, safely, once

situations.doing: holding a clearance and a stamp without bringing them together
situations.onArrival: it looks up and asks the vessel's name
situations.because: the clearance cannot be issued without a name and there are no ships
situations.offer: name a vessel and it will clear you out of anywhere

situations.doing: sitting on a corded chest at the top of the tide
situations.onArrival: he asks whether the tide has turned yet
situations.because: he has been waiting to sail since before you were born
situations.offer: tell him the tide and he will give you the chest and everything in it

situations.doing: carrying oil up to a light that is already burning
situations.onArrival: they hand you the can rather than pass
situations.because: the light is kept and cannot be let out
situations.offer: carry the oil up and the light will show you a way through anything

situations.doing: lying off the stair with her oars shipped
situations.onArrival: she comes in to the stair as you reach the bottom step
situations.because: she was pulled out for a vessel that never signalled
situations.offer: get aboard and the water opens to you where the quay does not

situations.doing: reading a book of clearances aloud to the water
situations.onArrival: it stops at a sailing with no return entered against it
situations.because: every vessel is entered out and in, and one never came in
situations.offer: supply the ending of that voyage and it will sign anything you ask

temptations.benefit: once, leave anywhere without being stopped
temptations.standingDrawback: you leave in the name on the paper, not your own

temptations.cue: oil out of the harbour light
temptations.benefit: once, be found by whatever is looking for you
temptations.standingDrawback: everything looking for you finds you, not only the friendly

temptations.benefit: know the true channel through anything here
temptations.standingDrawback: you know which channels were altered, and by whom

temptations.benefit: once, have what a traveller would have packed
temptations.standingDrawback: they packed it to leave, and still want to

temptations.benefit: once, be taken aboard anything on the water
temptations.standingDrawback: you are expected to bring the vessel back

tide.dangerLine: the harbour keeps time by the water and it is not going to wait for you

institution: a tide glass in the office window, turned by the watch
tide marks cut into every quay wall for two hundred years
a harbour that is a basin at high water and a mud flat at low
ritual: the glass turned at the top of every tide
the gates of the basin shut at the same point on the flood
a bell struck for the turn, twice
demand: a glass running out with nobody by it
a basin gate standing open on the flood
a tide mark reached and passed with nothing moving
wound: a glass left unturned and the sand all through
basin gates jammed open and the water gone
tide marks cut for years that never came
anchor: a tide table in one hand, correct to the minute
a gate that still shuts on the flood

features: a glass with the sand nearly through
a basin gate standing open
a tide mark freshly cut
a bell rope swinging after the turn
a tide table left open
water standing where it should not

decisions.cue: a tide glass running out with nobody by it to turn it
decisions.cost: turning it keeps the harbour's time going

resolve.success: you turn it at the right moment and the harbour keeps your time — one thing here waits for you
resolve.failure: you turn it late and the hour here is wrong for the rest of the delve: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: let it run out; the harbour stops keeping time and everything happens at once

decisions.cue: a basin gate standing open on the flood
decisions.cost: shutting it holds the water in; leaving it lets the basin drain

resolve.success: you shut the gate on the tide and the basin fills — the drowned street goes under and stays there
resolve.failure: you shut it with something still coming through: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: leave it open; the basin empties and the mud berth is walkable, both ways

decisions.cue: a tide mark cut fresh into a wall above the waterline
decisions.cost: somebody is still recording tides that do not happen

resolve.success: you read the marks and learn exactly when the harbour stopped, and what was in it
resolve.failure: you cut a mark of your own and the water rises to meet it
resolve.orElse: leave the wall; you will misjudge the water later, at the worst point

decisions.cue: a bell rope still swinging after a turn nobody struck
decisions.cost: the turn was struck by something

resolve.success: you strike the turn correctly and everything here that keeps time comes to order
resolve.failure: you strike it wrong and the harbour turns early, against you
resolve.orElse: leave the rope; nothing here agrees about what hour it is

decisions.cue: a tide table lying open, correct to the minute, in a dead man's hand
decisions.cost: the table is right and the harbour is wrong

resolve.success: you take the table and can predict every movement of the water here
resolve.failure: you take it and the hand closes: whatever kept it wants it back
resolve.orElse: leave it; you cross the mud on a guess

decisions.cue: water standing on a quay it should not reach for another six hours
decisions.cost: the harbour's tide is not the sea's any more

resolve.success: you work out what the harbour is keeping time to instead, and can use it
resolve.failure: you wade it, and what the water is standing over notices
resolve.orElse: go the long way round above the waterline, costing a Turn

situations.doing: turning a glass that has already run through
situations.onArrival: it asks what the hour is, and means the tide
situations.because: the glass is turned at the top of every tide and the tides stopped
situations.offer: give it an hour and it will hold the water back while you cross

situations.doing: standing at a basin gate with the winch bars in their hands
situations.onArrival: they look to you before they heave
situations.because: the gate shuts on the flood and the flood has not come
situations.offer: tell them to shut it and the basin fills, and the drowned street is closed

situations.doing: waiting on the mud with a boat that has nothing to float on
situations.onArrival: he asks how long until the water
situations.because: he came in on a tide that never went out again
situations.offer: tell him a time and he will put you across the harbour when it comes

situations.doing: cutting a tide mark into a wall well above the water
situations.onArrival: it steps back and asks whether that looks right to you
situations.because: the marks are cut for tides the harbour still expects
situations.offer: agree with the mark and the water will rise for you, once, where you need it

situations.doing: hanging in a frame on the quay head with the rope still moving
situations.onArrival: the rope stops when you take hold of it
situations.because: the turn was struck and nobody struck it
situations.offer: strike the turn properly and everything here that keeps time obeys you

situations.doing: lying full at a state of tide that cannot be happening
situations.onArrival: the water is dead flat and there is a good breeze
situations.because: the harbour keeps its own time now and will not be corrected
situations.offer: name the true hour aloud and the water goes back to the sea's time

temptations.benefit: once, make something happen exactly when you say
temptations.standingDrawback: the harbour's time is yours and everyone else's is wrong

temptations.benefit: know when the water will do anything here
temptations.standingDrawback: you also know how little time you have

temptations.cue: a winch bar off the basin gate
temptations.benefit: once, hold or release the water
temptations.standingDrawback: whatever the water covers is uncovered, or the reverse

temptations.cue: a clapper out of the quay bell
temptations.benefit: once, call the turn and be obeyed
temptations.standingDrawback: nothing here can strike the true turn while you hold it

temptations.cue: a chisel from the tide-cutter's belt
temptations.benefit: once, set where the water stops
temptations.standingDrawback: the water treats the mark as a promise

wreck.dangerLine: the harbour lost a ship in its own roads and has never once admitted it

institution: a hall hung with the boards of every vessel lost off this coast
a bell buoy moored over a wreck in the fairway
a burial ground for the ones who came ashore unnamed
ritual: a name read out and a board hung for every ship that does not return
the bell buoy answered from the shore each night
the drowned laid out on the quay and given names if anyone can
demand: a board hung blank in a hall where every other board is lettered
a bell buoy sounding with no sea running
a grave dug and left open above the tideline
wound: boards taken down and burnt in one night
a wreck in the fairway with no mark over it at all
the drowned buried unnamed, all of them, in a hurry
anchor: the bell off the ship that went down in the roads
a list of the lost with every name written
a board lettered for a ship the harbour denies

features: a blank board in a hall of lettered ones
a grave dug open above the tideline
a bell sounding with no sea running
charred boards in a grate
a list of the lost with a gap
wreckage stacked and sorted

decisions.cue: a board hung blank in a hall where every other board is lettered
decisions.cost: lettering it admits the loss

resolve.success: you letter the board with the right name and the Trinity Brethren give you everything they have
resolve.failure: you letter it wrongly and a ship that came home is entered as lost: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it blank; the harbour goes on denying the wreck and so does everything in it

decisions.cue: a bell buoy sounding out in the roads with no sea running
decisions.cost: something is moving it

resolve.success: you answer the bell from the shore, properly, and what is under it comes up to talk
resolve.failure: you go out to it and it stops sounding while you are alongside
resolve.orElse: let it ring; it rings all night, and the drowned come in on the tide

decisions.cue: a grave dug open above the tideline with nobody in it
decisions.cost: filling it needs a name and a body

resolve.success: you name whoever it was cut for and the ground here settles, and lets you pass
resolve.failure: you fill it with anything else and the ground takes exception: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: leave it open; the burial ground stays restless behind you

decisions.cue: charred boards in a grate with the lettering half readable
decisions.cost: somebody burnt the record of what was lost

resolve.success: you read enough off the char to name the ship the harbour denies
resolve.failure: you are found reading it by something that helped burn them
resolve.orElse: leave the grate; the ship's name is never established

decisions.cue: a list of the lost with every name written and one line short
decisions.cost: the missing name is the one that matters

resolve.success: you match the gap against {priorCue} and have the name for the ending
resolve.failure: you write in a guess and the list accepts it, and it is wrong
resolve.orElse: leave the gap; the ending is fought rather than answered

decisions.cue: wreckage stacked and sorted on the quay by size, not by ship
decisions.cost: somebody has been keeping it, not selling it

resolve.success: you find the piece with the ship's name on it, which is what the sorter was hiding
resolve.failure: you disturb the stack and the sorter comes to see who is in their yard
resolve.orElse: leave the stack; the only proof of the wreck stays buried in it

situations.doing: holding a blank board up against a wall of lettered ones
situations.onArrival: it asks you what name goes on it
situations.because: the board must be hung and nobody would say the name
situations.offer: give it the name and it will open the light and everything under it

situations.doing: lying in a row on the quay with their hands crossed
situations.onArrival: the nearest turns its head as your shadow falls on it
situations.because: they came ashore unnamed and were buried unnamed
situations.offer: name any one of them and they will carry you across the harbour

situations.doing: sorting salvage into piles by size in a locked yard
situations.onArrival: they stop and ask what you are looking for, without hiding anything
situations.because: nobody has come for any of it in living memory
situations.offer: tell them and they will find it, and tell you what ship it came off

situations.doing: standing at an open grave above the tideline with a spade
situations.onArrival: it asks whether you know who this one was
situations.because: the grave was cut for somebody who never came ashore
situations.offer: give it a name and it will fill the grave and let you through the ground

situations.doing: sounding steadily out in flat calm water
situations.onArrival: the sounding changes when you come to the quay edge
situations.because: it is moored over a wreck the harbour will not mark on any chart
situations.offer: answer it and what is under it will tell you what happened here

situations.doing: standing in a hall of boards with one wall bare
situations.onArrival: they part to let you at the bare wall
situations.because: the boards on that wall were burnt in a night
situations.offer: letter one board and the whole hall will vouch for you

temptations.benefit: once, make a loss be admitted
temptations.standingDrawback: everything drowned here hears it and comes to be counted

temptations.cue: a lettered board off the hall wall
temptations.benefit: once, prove a ship was lost and when
temptations.standingDrawback: the ship it names is unaccounted for again

temptations.benefit: once, be recognised by any of the drowned
temptations.standingDrawback: they recognise you as one of the crew

temptations.benefit: know every name the sea took here
temptations.standingDrawback: the gap in it is a name that wants filling

temptations.benefit: once, put something to rest
temptations.standingDrawback: the ground opens for you wherever you carry it
